guard: a breaking change that lands with no matching section in docs/UPGRADING.md is refused, while a breaking change WITH its section and a non-breaking change with no section both pass
why: Cotal #1578: 0.49.0 changed how a credential's authority is recorded, the repository carried no UPGRADING.md, and an operator with a live 30-agent deployment could not tell whether their credentials survived or which side of a split topology to upgrade first. Nothing in CI noticed. This gate is what notices.

A gate like this has two ways to be useless and each needs its own mutation. It can stop DETECTING, in which case the breaking change sails through and the operator is back where the issue started. Or it can start firing on EVERYTHING, in which case it is turned off within a week and the first failure mode returns by another route. M1 and M2 are those two directions.

M3 and M4 attack the two readers rather than the verdict. A marker reader that never fires and a section reader that always finds coverage both leave the verdict logic perfectly correct and grading nothing, which is the shape this repository has been catching all week: the gate is armed, and its accept control returns zero.

M5 is the cheapest way to satisfy a gate that only checked whether the file was touched. If an empty heading counted, the rule would decay into adding a heading at release time, and the document would stop being the thing the reporter actually needed.
The self-test drives the real exported functions in the mutated file, so the code under test is the gate itself and not a copy of its logic.

M1 and the too-wide case were separate mutations until the predicate tightened and collapsed them onto one line. They are merged rather than both kept: two names over one mutation is one claim counted twice. The too-wide behaviour is still graded, by the cell M1 reddens and by the dedicated TOO WIDE cell beside it.

mutations.name: M1 the coverage predicate stops refusing: a breaking change with no new section passes
mutations.find:
if (addedSections.length === 0)
    return { ok: false, reason: `${breaking.length} breaking change(s) and no new ${UPGRADING_PATH} section in the same range` };
mutations.replace:
if (addedSections.length === 0)
    return { ok: true, reason: `${breaking.length} breaking change(s) and no new ${UPGRADING_PATH} section in the same range` };
mutations.expectRed: ACCEPT CONTROL: a breaking change with no new UPGRADING.md section is REFUSED
mutations.cell: ACCEPT CONTROL: a breaking change with no new UPGRADING.md section is REFUSED
mutations.note: THE DEFECT THIS GATE SHIPPED WITH AT ITS FIRST HEAD, so this is a revert-check and not a contrived edit. Two separate mutations used to live here, one for 'no edit at all' and one for 'an edit that added no section'. Tightening the predicate from `upgradingChanged` to `addedSections` COLLAPSED THEM ONTO ONE LINE, and keeping both would have been one claim counted twice, which is the defect this repository has been naming all day. They are merged, and the too-wide case is graded by its own CELL rather than by a duplicate mutant. Measured through the real CLI before the fix: a `feat(core)!` commit beside a ONE-LINE TYPO FIX on the page passed as 'covered by 8 section(s)', every one of them written for an earlier release; and it decays, because each section the page accumulates becomes permanent pre-coverage for every future break.

mutations.name: M2 the gate fires on everything: a non-breaking change is refused too
mutations.find: if (breaking.length === 0) return { ok: true, reason: "no breaking commits DETECTED in range (unmarked breaks are invisible to this check)" };
mutations.replace: if (breaking.length === 0 && addedSections.length > 0) return { ok: true, reason: "no breaking commits DETECTED in range (unmarked breaks are invisible to this check)" };
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE CONTROL: a NON-breaking change with no section passes (not vacuously red)
mutations.cell: REFUSE CONTROL: a NON-breaking change with no section passes (not vacuously red)
mutations.note: The other failure direction, and the one that kills the gate socially rather than technically. Both accept cells stay GREEN under this mutation, so only the third leg catches it: without that leg, 'detects breaking changes' and 'reds on every changeset' are the same measurement.

mutations.name: M3 the breaking-marker reader never fires on a conventional `!`
mutations.expectRed: a `!` in the conventional type is read as breaking
mutations.cell: a `!` in the conventional type is read as breaking
mutations.note: The verdict logic is untouched and perfectly correct under this mutation; it is simply never handed a positive. That is the exact shape of an armed gate grading nothing, and it is invisible to any cell that only exercises the verdict.

mutations.name: M4 the section reader counts the page's own structural headings as coverage
mutations.expectRed: …and excludes the page's own structural headings
mutations.cell: …and excludes the page's own structural headings
mutations.note: With this mutation the page's permanent furniture (the contract section and the how-to-add-a-section section) counts as a release section forever, so every future breaking change is pre-covered by headings nobody wrote for it.

mutations.name: M5 an empty heading counts as an upgrade section
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE CONTROL: an empty section is not coverage
mutations.cell: REFUSE CONTROL: an empty section is not coverage
mutations.note: The cheapest possible way to satisfy the rule without doing the work. A heading with nothing under it tells an operator nothing, and a gate that accepts one teaches the release process to add headings rather than write upgrade notes.

mutations.name: M6 the section difference becomes a head-only read
mutations.find:
const before = new Set(coveringSections(basePage));
  return coveringSections(headPage).filter((s) => !before.has(s));
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE CONTROL: rewording an EXISTING section adds no new section
mutations.cell: REFUSE CONTROL: rewording an EXISTING section adds no new section
mutations.note: The same defect as M1 one layer down: a head-only read answers "does the page have sections", which every page does forever after its first release, instead of "did THIS range write one". It also silently breaks the historical replay, since reading only the head of an old range is how a gate reports a green that belongs to today. THIS MUTANT SURVIVED THE WHOLE SUITE on its first run, with the tool's positive control proving the suite reached the file and simply did not test that line, because the difference was computed INLINE IN THE CLI where no cell could call it. That is why it is now the exported addedSectionsBetween: a predicate the suite cannot call is a predicate nothing grades.

mutations.name: M7 a section that names no release counts as coverage
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE CONTROL: an unnamed section on a real page is not counted
mutations.cell: REFUSE CONTROL: an unnamed section on a real page is not counted
mutations.note: The residue of M5 after empty headings were excluded. If a heading need not name its release, the cheapest way to satisfy the gate becomes a section called `Notes` with one sentence under it, or an unrelated heading that happened to arrive in the same range. Coverage is CLAIMED BY A HEADING, so a heading that names no release claims everything and distinguishes nothing. Requiring a version token also makes the section the one an operator upgrading that release will actually search for.

mutations.name: M8 a crash is reported as a refusal: misuse exits 1
mutations.find:
console.error("This is a MISUSE exit (2), not a refusal: nothing was graded. Check the --base/--range refs exist.");
    process.exit(2);
mutations.replace:
console.error("This is a MISUSE exit (2), not a refusal: nothing was graded. Check the --base/--range refs exist.");
    process.exit(1);
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 on an unresolvable ref: misuse is never reported as a refusal
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 on an unresolvable ref: misuse is never reported as a refusal
mutations.note: ALSO A REVERT-CHECK RATHER THAN A CONTRIVED EDIT: the first head of this gate threw out of the top level on a mistyped ref and exited 1, the refusal code, so a CI job with a bad base ref would have reported 'a breaking change is missing its UPGRADING.md section' while having graded NOTHING. That is worse than a crash, because it is a false verdict in the accusing direction and the fix a reader would attempt is to write a section that was never missing. The exit codes are now graded by cells that run the real CLI in a subprocess, with both directions controlled: a genuine refusal must still be 1 and a clean range still 0, so a mutation cannot satisfy the misuse cells by making every exit 2.

mutations.name: M9 a section whose body is only subsection headings counts as coverage
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE CONTROL: a section whose body is only SUBSECTION HEADINGS is not coverage
mutations.cell: REFUSE CONTROL: a section whose body is only SUBSECTION HEADINGS is not coverage
mutations.note: THE DEFECT THIS GATE SHIPPED AT ITS SECOND HEAD, found by reviewers and not by me, so it is a revert-check. `##` opened a section and every OTHER heading fell through to the body accumulator, so `## From 0.49.0 to 0.50.0` followed by nothing but `### What changed` satisfied `body.trim().length > 0` and was ACCEPTED. It is M5 one nesting level down, and none of the 33 cells walked it because M5's fixture page has no subsections: the suite graded the rule I was thinking about when I wrote M5. The mutation keeps a syntactically valid guard that can never match a real heading, so it restores the defect without disabling the line, which a reader would spot. Note the replacement must not simply delete the guard: the accompanying ACCEPT CONTROL cell (real prose under a subsection is still coverage) is what proves the fix did not over-correct into refusing every section that uses subsections.

mutations.name: M10 a truncated history is graded as though it were complete
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 in a SHALLOW repository: a truncated history is misuse, never a silent pass
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 in a SHALLOW repository: a truncated history is misuse, never a silent pass
mutations.note: MEASURED ON A REAL SHALLOW CLONE RATHER THAN ARGUED. actions/checkout defaults to depth 1, and the smoke job that runs this suite took that default. In a depth-1 checkout the tags v0.48.2 and v0.49.0 both still RESOLVE, so `git log` succeeds and returns a truncated set: the range holding 173 commits and two marked breaking changes reports as 1 commit and zero breaking changes, and the gate printed OK and exited 0. That is the exact sin this gate exists to catch, committed by the gate itself: a green meaning 'I could not see' on the check whose green is supposed to mean 'somebody documented the break'. The guard makes it a MISUSE exit instead, and the paired ACCEPT CONTROL (same command, full history, still exits 0) is what proves the guard discriminates rather than refusing everything.

mutations.name: M11 the suite declares itself ungraded on a repository that is fine
mutations.expectRed: cells are only skipped when THIS repository is genuinely shallow
mutations.cell: cells are only skipped when THIS repository is genuinely shallow
mutations.note: A SKIP IS A CLAIM AND IT NEEDS GRADING LIKE ANY OTHER. The skip path exists so a shallow checkout reports UNGRADED instead of a false red, but the same mechanism could silently drop real cells on a healthy repository, and the sentinel cannot catch that because pass+fail+skipped is invariant under a skip. This mutant forces the probe true on a full clone; the discriminating cell reds because it asserts the probe answers false in a full source and true only in a depth-1 clone. That cell is what stops the skip from becoming a way to make the suite quiet.

mutations.name: M12 --merge-snapshot accepts a checkout that is not a merge
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 on --merge-snapshot outside a two-parent merge: HEAD^1 is not a merge base
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 on --merge-snapshot outside a two-parent merge: HEAD^1 is not a merge base
mutations.note: THIS IS THE MUTANT FOR THE DEFECT THAT SHIPPED. On a single-parent checkout HEAD^1 is the branch's previous commit rather than the merge base, so the graded range shrinks to the last commit and a breaking change behind it reads as absent. The gate then prints OK and exits 0 on exactly the branch it exists to refuse: a clean green meaning I looked at the wrong thing. Reviewed against the caller's own parent check, which catches the same shape; the guard is duplicated deliberately, because a guard living only in its caller protects only the callers that remember it, and a local hook or a future workflow inherits none of that care.

mutations.name: M13 an explicit range silently overrides the merge snapshot's own range
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 when --merge-snapshot is combined with an explicit range: one range, one source
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 when --merge-snapshot is combined with an explicit range: one range, one source
mutations.note: TWO SOURCES FOR ONE RANGE IS THE DEFECT THIS WHOLE FLAG REPLACES. If both are accepted, the later assignment wins silently and a caller that passes both gets whichever the implementation happens to prefer, which is how a base from one snapshot ended up paired with a head from another in the first place. Refusing the combination keeps the range's provenance single and visible.

mutations.name: M14 an option that is given no value falls through and grades anyway
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 when --range is given no value: a dropped argument is misuse, not a pass
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 when --range is given no value: a dropped argument is misuse, not a pass
mutations.note: MEASURED AS A LIVE DEFECT, NOT IMAGINED. The original parser read an option value by looking one slot to the right without checking that a slot held one. A value-less --range read undefined, which is falsy, so the combination refusal never fired and the tool graded the merge snapshot and exited 0. A gate that greens on a typo is the decoration this tool exists to remove.

mutations.name: M15 an unknown argument is ignored rather than refused
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 on an UNKNOWN flag: an argument this tool does not understand is never ignored
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 on an UNKNOWN flag: an argument this tool does not understand is never ignored
mutations.note: A misspelled flag must never be silently dropped. Measured before the fix: --merge-snapshot --bogus graded and exited 0, so a caller who mistyped an argument got a pass for a run that ignored what they asked for.

mutations.name: M16 the merge-snapshot cells read the ambient checkout instead of a repository they build
mutations.find: const linear = build("linear", "feat(core)!: rename a wire field");
mutations.expectRed: EXIT 2 on --merge-snapshot outside a two-parent merge: HEAD^1 is not a merge base
mutations.cell: EXIT 2 on --merge-snapshot outside a two-parent merge: HEAD^1 is not a merge base
mutations.note: THIS IS THE DEFECT THAT TOOK THE SUITE RED IN CI. The cell used to run against whatever checkout the suite was in, so its result was decided by that checkout parent count: 42 passed on a branch head, 41 passed 1 failed on the pull request merge ref, which is exactly what CI checks out at fetch-depth 0. The mutation proof then refused to grade against a red baseline and all 13 mutants went UNGRADED. A cell must build the condition it names.

mutations.name: the detector hard-codes the job name instead of honouring the one passed in
mutations.find:
return candidates.filter((j) => j !== hostJob
    && new RegExp
mutations.cell: the host job is honoured rather than assumed: `unit` is not stale when `unit` runs it
mutations.expectRed: the host job is honoured rather than assumed
mutations.note: A detector that assumes the answer cannot notice the step moving, which is the only thing it exists to notice.

mutations.name: the stale-claim detector returns nothing, so every page reads as clean
mutations.find:
return candidates.filter((j) => j !== hostJob
    && new RegExp(`(runs?|grades?|grading path is|step in|in) the .${j}. job`).test(text));
mutations.cell: ACCEPT CONTROL: a page claiming a job that no longer runs the gate is NAMED
mutations.expectRed: ACCEPT CONTROL: a page claiming a job that no longer runs the gate is NAMED
mutations.note: This is the shape that actually shipped: one paragraph correct, another still naming `unit`. Pinned against BUILT documents rather than the live ones, because when the real docs are clean a disabled detector is unobservable: the live-file version of this mutation SURVIVED.

mutations.name: the bundle-shaped cell is stubbed true, so the generated copy is graded by nothing
mutations.find: cell("ACCEPT CONTROL: a stale claim inside a BUNDLE-shaped escaped string is NAMED",
mutations.replace: cell("ACCEPT CONTROL: a stale claim inside a BUNDLE-shaped escaped string is NAMED", true) || cell("dead",
mutations.cell: ACCEPT CONTROL: a stale claim inside a BUNDLE-shaped escaped string is NAMED
mutations.expectRed: every cell ran or was reported ungraded
mutations.note: The bundle is the copy connector-core serves to users, stored as one escaped JSON string. A reader written for the markdown can pass on the source and miss the generated copy, which is the half that reaches users. Stubbing the cell trips the cell-count sentinel, so the suite refuses rather than quietly grading one artefact less.

mutations.name: an absent candidate list silently falls back to a hard-coded pair
mutations.find:
if (!Array.isArray(candidates) || candidates.length === 0)
    throw new Error("staleJobClaims: candidates must be a non-empty array of job names read from the workflows");
mutations.cell: REFUSE CONTROL: grading with no candidate list is a refusal, not a clean page
mutations.expectRed: REFUSE CONTROL: grading with no candidate list is a refusal, not a clean page
mutations.note: Found by review end to end: with a hard-coded pair, a page naming the CORRECT host AND ALSO a false third job passes everything, because the positive check is satisfied while the refuse leg never looks at the third. A silent default is how that list stops tracking the workflows, so the absence must throw rather than guess.
